newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA PROTESTERS DISRUPT BOMBAY RAILWAY SERVICES.
newsitem.headline: INDIA PROTESTERS DISRUPT BOMBAY RAILWAY SERVICES.

text.p: Angry commuters squatted on the tracks at a suburban railway station to paralyse train services into India's commercial capital on Thursday, authorities said.

"Trains to and from Thane have been disrupted since 9.30 a.m. (0400 GMT)," said Jagdish Prasad, a spokesman for the Central Railway network. Thane, about 25 kms northeast of Bombay, is a major rail terminus.
"People have blocked all four tracks, and trains cannot arrive or leave," he added. Prasad said he had no estimate of how long the agitation would continue.
The spokesman said the agitation started because regular travellers from Thane had become enraged over the shortage of seats in trains scheduled to start from Thane.
"There have been no reports of violence or stone-throwing so far," he added. "We expect services to return to normal soon."
